verdict.rationale: Google's docs say codes sync across devices through the user's Google Account and appear automatically when signing in on a new device, which covers simultaneous phone and tablet use. Nothing in the evidence shows a desktop or computer client, and the GitHub project describes only mobile-platform implementations, so the 'computer' part of the story is unevidenced. Missing for 10: evidence of a desktop/computer client receiving synced codes, independent hands-on confirmation of real-time multi-device sync, and detail on sync behavior (e.g., propagation of edits and deletions).

support.subject: As an everyday user, my tokens are available on my phone, tablet, and computer at the same time, kept in sync automatically

citations.quote: With Google Authenticator, you can synchronize your verification codes across all your devices, simply by signing in to your Google Account.
When you sign in to your Google Account within Google Authenticator on a new device, your codes are automatically synced to this device.
The Google Authenticator project includes implementations of one-time passcode generators for several mobile platforms.
